reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Evidence shows target engagement through ELISPOT assays detecting immune responses in peripheral blood and sentinel nodes. The GM-CSF arm showed superior immune responses (8/27 responders in sentinel nodes vs 1/13 in dendritic cell arm, p=0.004), confirming the vaccine components engaged their intended targets (gp100, tyrosinase antigens). 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Downstream biology was modulated as evidenced by tumor-antigen-specific immunity development, particularly in the GM-CSF arm. The significant difference in sentinel node immune responses (p=0.004) demonstrates pathway activation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite confirmed target engagement and pathway modulation, clinical translation failed. Overall response rate was only 7.5% (3/40 patients achieved partial response), with no complete responses in either arm. The primary endpoint of objective clinical response was not met. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No significant subgroup differences in clinical response were observed, though the GM-CSF arm showed superior immune responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a small study (n=40) comparing two vaccine formulations rather than vaccine vs control, which may have limited power to detect clinical benefit.

failure_modes.evidence: Target engagement confirmed by ELISPOT assays, pathway modulation demonstrated by tumor-antigen-specific immunity (especially in GM-CSF arm with p=0.004 for sentinel node responses), but clinical endpoint failed with only 7.5% overall response rate and no complete responses
